what_its_for: Topiramate is used to help prevent seizures in people with epilepsy. It is also used to prevent migraine headaches (it does not treat a migraine that has already started). In some cases, it is used together with other medicines to help with weight loss.
how_to_take: Take topiramate exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush, break, or chew them, as this can cause a bitter taste and affect how the medicine works. If you are taking the extended-release capsules (Trokendi XR or Qudexy XR), swallow them whole. Qudexy XR capsules can also be opened and sprinkled on a small spoonful of soft food like applesauce — swallow right away without chewing. Drink plenty of water every day while taking this medicine to help protect your kidneys from developing kidney stones.
dosing: Your doctor will usually start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over several weeks. This helps reduce side effects. The typical starting dose is 25 mg once or twice a day. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on your condition and how you respond to the medicine. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store topiramate at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from moisture, heat, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of the reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medicine properly — ask your pharmacist about local medication take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking topiramate, as it can increase dizziness and confusion. Be careful driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid becoming overheated or dehydrated — drink plenty of fluids, especially in hot weather or during exercise. Avoid a high-fat, low-carbohydrate (ketogenic) diet unless your doctor specifically approves it. If you are a woman of childbearing age, talk to your doctor about reliable birth control, as topiramate can make some hormonal birth control pills less effective and can cause serious harm to an unborn baby.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of suicide or self-harm, unusual changes in mood or behavior, decreased sweating with a high fever (especially in children), sudden eye pain or vision changes (could be a sign of glaucoma), severe muscle pain or weakness, signs of kidney stones such as severe back or side pain, blood in urine, or painful urination, signs of high acid levels in the blood (rapid breathing, tiredness, loss of appetite, confusion), or a skin rash. Also call your doctor if your seizures get worse or if you feel dizzy, have memory problems, or trouble concentrating that is bothering your daily life.
when_it_works: For seizure prevention, it may take several weeks before topiramate reaches its full effect as the dose is gradually increased. For migraine prevention, it may take 2 to 3 months of regular use to notice a significant reduction in headaches. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause withdrawal seizures even if you do not have epilepsy.
special_populations: Children: Topiramate can be used in children as young as 2 years old for certain conditions, but the dose is based on body weight. Watch children closely for decreased sweating and overheating. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness and confusion — use with extra caution. Kidney problems: Your doctor may need to lower your dose if you have kidney disease. Pregnancy: Topiramate can cause serious birth defects, including cleft lip and cleft palate, and low birth weight. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control. Discuss the risks and benefits carefully with your doctor before or if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Topiramate passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor about whether it is safe to breastfeed while taking this medicine.
